content.introduction: This week, Wall Street is closely watching earnings from several major tech companies. The "Magnificent Seven" will see earnings reports from four companies: Microsoft, Meta, Amazon, and Apple. Investors are particularly focused on capital expenditures, especially in relation to AI investments. The Nasdaq experienced a drop, testing June lows, which will also be a key focus this week. The earnings reports from these companies are expected to provide significant insights into the tech sector's performance and future strategies.
body:
So, that will again come into focus when viewing the big tech earnings this week - where four of the 'Magnificent Seven' will report. Here are some of the big names to watch out for this week:

 27 July: AstraZeneca
 28 July: Boeing, Visa, Coca-Cola
 29 July: Microsoft, Meta, Arm Holdings, Qualcomm
 30 July: Amazon, Apple, Mastercard, Shell
 31 July: ExxonMobil, Chevron [...] As a reminder, Nvidia will only report in late August so this week will pretty much be key in deciding the fate of big tech after back-to-back weekly drops in the Nasdaq. The drop on Friday brought the index down to 24,975 in testing the June lows, which will be a key focus point this week despite the early bounce today.

There's always something new to learn about the markets. Explore investingLive's educational video collection for quick explanations and useful insights. [...] There's going to be quite a lot for markets to digest in the week ahead. US-Iran developments are already making waves to start the new week but keep in mind that there will also be major central bank decisions and month-end trading to deal with. Adding to the mix in the days to come will be big tech earnings in the US.

After the setback from Alphabet (Google) last week, it's free game now even though US futures may be pointing up to start the week.

Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon announce quarterly results this week. While they all have very different businesses – and compete in certain areas – Wall Street is going to be laser focused on one particular line item: capital expenditures. [...] The other megacap company reporting this week is Apple. The iPhone maker has thus far been in a separate category in AI because it doesn't operate a public cloud service or build major large language models that it shares with the public.

However, Apple CEO Tim Cook said in June that the company would be increasing its capital expenditures for AI, so it's likely to be a bigger topic in Thursday's earnings report. [...] Key Points

 Microsoft, Meta and Alphabet report quarterly results on Wednesday, followed by Amazon and Apple on Thursday.
 Investors are particularly focused on capital expenditures, as they look closely to see how the companies are planning AI investments.
 OpenAI, which is privately held, has announced about $1 trillion worth of AI infrastructure buildout plans in recent months.

Microsoft, Alphabet, Meta and Amazon announce quarterly results this week. While they all have very different businesses – and compete in certain areas – Wall Street is going to be laser focused on one particular line item: capital expenditures. [...] The other megacap company reporting this week is Apple. The iPhone maker has thus far been in a separate category in AI because it doesn't operate a public cloud service or build major large language models that it shares with the public.

However, Apple CEO Tim Cook said in June that the company would be increasing its capital expenditures for AI, so it's likely to be a bigger topic in Thursday's earnings report. [...] Aside from OpenAI, the biggest builders include the four internet hyperscalers that are set to post earnings this week. In each case, investors want to see aggressive plans and a clear strategy. But unlike OpenAI, they can't go too big out of concern that public investors will hammer their stocks.

Morgan Stanley analysts said in a note last week that they expect total hyperscaler capital expenditures to grow 24% next year to nearly $550 billion.
